name: marquee-markdown
tagline: A terminal markdown reader with a contents pane that knows where you are.
summary: A glow-compatible reader that renders markdown the way a document viewer does: a centred reading column on a painted page, typographic headings, sealed code cards, box-drawn tables, and a table-of-contents pane that tracks the scroll and folds sections. It reads files, directories, standard input, URLs and github.com/owner/repo, reloads on save, searches in place, and ships ten themes as TOML data. Linux, macOS and Windows.

swe.angle: A 27k-line Rust TUI with 897 tests and sixteen releases: a markdown renderer written against a cell grid, packaged for crates.io, Homebrew and Scoop, with a nixpkgs submission in review.

highlights: Renders the HTML inside a README too: a centred <h1> becomes a heading in the contents pane, badge images become the links they advertise, a <details> block opens with its summary as the title.
The contents pane tracks the scroll and folds sections, the feature glow has no equivalent of and the reason the project exists.
Themes are data: ten shipped as TOML, so a new palette needs no Rust and no recompile.
Keeps glow's flags and keys so muscle memory carries over; every key is rebindable from one config file.
The README screenshot is regenerated by a script from the renderer's own output, so the picture cannot drift from the program.
